enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
648 AM MDT Thu Oct 29 2026

...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... Updated at 645 AM MDT Thu Oct 29 2026

 - Showers and thunderstorms will arrive in two batches today,
   starting with the afternoon, and then sweeping west to east
   overnight. Additional storms will work into SW New Mexico on
   Friday afternoon, weakening as they drift east Friday night.
   Localized flash flooding will be possible.

 - A quiet period looks to arrive in time for Halloween, 
   Saturday.

 - A upper level system will bring more showers and thunderstorms
   to the area Sunday and into Monday. 

 - Quieter and drier weather looks to prevail next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1012 PM MDT Wed Oct 28 2026

Southwest flow aloft is increasing as upper low nears the California 
coast...and several short waves out ahead of the low near Baja
rotate east toward New Mexico. This flow will bring up existing 
sub-tropical moisture over northern Mexico, including some 
moisture from TS Vance, across the CWA Thursday. PWs approach one
inch from the RG Valley east. Batted around a flood watch but 
decided not to issue one. The moisture, decent instability and 
slow storm movement could still create a few flooding storms. 

One of the short waves rotating out of the California trough reaches 
New Mexico late FRIDAY afternoon and into the evening to spread 
another round of showers/storms to the area. PWs almost as high as 
Thursday's event, with sub-tropical jet approaching and drawing in 
moisture from the eastern Pacific. Shear environment looks better 
than Thursday, and along with modest CAPE values may be more 
conducive to some strong/severe storms. The negative is that the 
storms are not likely to start until late in the day. 

SATURDAY (Halloween) looks to be a tweener day as the short wave 
exits the area and we await the the west coast upper low. Both 
GFS/ECMWF dampen the low as it approaches, but phasing it in with 
the Pac NW over the Great Basin SUNDAY. This looks to be a fast 
moving feature, though ECMWF somewhat slower. GFS moves it out by 
late Sunday night while the ECMWF lets it hang around until Monday 
afternoon. Showers/storms should start out west Sunday afternoon and 
spread east through the evening hours. Once again PWs approach or 
slightly exceed one inch, suggesting some flood potential. 
However mid-level storm motion winds of 30-50 mph may not allow 
for prolonged rain over any specific area. 

Main Pacific cold front moves through late Sunday night with 
secondary colder front dropping out of the Great Basin to the CWA 
Monday night. High temps by Tuesday may remain in the 60s across the 
lowlands. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 644 AM MDT Thu Oct 29 2026

VFR conditions prevailing, but afternoon thunderstorms will
develop around desert mountain ranges this afternoon, with another
round sweeping through later tonight. Ceilings could drop to
around 5000-6000 feet in thunderstorms, with brief IFR visibility.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 644 AM MDT Thu Oct 29 2026

Low fire weather concerns will continue through the next several
days as an unsettled weather pattern brings more rain chances to
the region. Temperatures will run near normal through the weekend,
while minimum RH values will be quite elevated -- dropping only 
into the 35 to 45 percent range in the lowlands, and higher values
in the the mountains. Lighter low level winds will cause vent 
rates to suffer in parts of the Tularosa Basin today, and over the 
entire area on Friday.

&&
